intro: Utah runs its elections county by county, through each county clerk.

id_rule.text: For in-person voting, show one valid photo ID with your name, such as a Utah driver license, a state or U.S. government ID, a U.S. passport, a U.S. military ID, or a tribal ID (a tribal ID does not need a photo). Or show two documents that together prove your name and where you live.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: 7:00 am to 8:00 pm (at vote centers; counties may vary)
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Ballots mailed to every active voter
dates.detail: Utah is an all-mail state. A ballot is mailed to each active registered voter, and you do not need to ask for one.

dates.label: Early in-person voting may begin
dates.detail: State law lets early voting start up to 14 days before Election Day, for at least four days. Each county sets its own days, hours and places, so check with your county clerk.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: Your registration must reach your county clerk by 5 pm. After this date you can still register and vote in person at a vote center on Election Day with two forms of valid ID.

dates.label: Last day to request a mail ballot
dates.detail: Request a ballot by 5 pm. This does not apply to military and overseas voters, who have a different deadline.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Return your mail ballot to a drop box or a vote center, or mail it. It must be received by your clerk by 8 pm, so a postmark is not enough. Vote centers are open 7 am to 8 pm.
